summary: Feed s115_double is degraded: IDS port overloaded by microbursts (1.71 Gbps peak on 1 Gbps port, 7 intervals) and encrypted traffic share 71.8% exceeds 60% tolerance for full-payload inspection.

findings.root_cause: Microburst traffic from packet broker exceeds IDS ingress capacity: 1.71 Gbps peak in 1ms burst vs 1 Gbps port (171% of capacity) across 7 intervals. Likely aggregated/bursty forwarding without load-balancing or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS will drop packets at ingress during bursts, causing missed signatures, broken flow reassembly and blind spots for detection despite needing both directions and full payload.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute bursts across 2+ IDS ports or a load-balanced IDS cluster to keep per-port utilization below 80% and prevent tail drops during 1.7 Gbps peaks.

findings.root_cause: 71.8% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/QUIC) vs 60% tolerance for this IDS. Feed is delivering mostly opaque payloads that the IDS cannot inspect without decryption.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS requires full payload for signature matching; with 72% encrypted, detection coverage drops sharply - malware, C2 and exploit payloads inside TLS remain invisible, increasing false negatives.

params.method: out-of-band TLS 1.2/1.3 decryption with key share or forward proxy

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS sessions at the packet broker before the IDS or selectively bypass trusted encrypted flows to bring inspectable traffic back under 60% threshold and restore payload visibility.
